reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Phase 03 misread the code architecture. The sync path DOES validate array lengths via verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs before block acceptance. Flow: (1) request_manager.nim:437 adds columns to quarantine without validation (standard quarantine pattern), (2) request_manager.nim:444 calls blockVerifier, (3) block_processor.nim:254 (backfill) or line 687 (normal) calls verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs which passes all arrays (kzg_commitments, column, kzg_proofs, cellIndices) to verifyCellKzgProofBatch. The crypto library enforces equal-length constraints for batch verification. The claim that 'sync path only checks inclusion proof and never calls verify_data_column_sidecar' is factually incorrect—validation occurs at block processing time, not at receipt time. This is architecturally sound: quarantine accepts unvalidated data, then validates during processing. Spec reference from 01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json line 244-260: invariant requires 'len(sidecar.column) == len(sidecar.kzg_commitments) == len(sidecar.kzg_proofs)', which IS enforced by the existing validation in block_processor.nim.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: 01e invariant PROP-6a4369e9-inv-010: 'Column, kzg_commitments, and kzg_proofs arrays must all have equal length.' Code enforces this via verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs at block processing.
